Back Extra: Why: anatomists call the elbow-to-wrist segment the forearm, so 'arm' means only the upper segment.

Text: The humerus articulates proximally with the {{c1::scapula (glenoid cavity)}} and distally with the {{c2::radius and ulna}}.
Back Extra:
Why: the humerus's rounded head fits the glenoid cavity at the shoulder, and its capitulum and trochlea meet the forearm bones at the elbow.

Pitfall: the manual says the humerus also articulates with the clavicle; it doesn't. The clavicle meets only the acromion and the sternum.

Text: The head of the humerus points {{c1::medially}}.
Back Extra:
Why: the head has to face the glenoid cavity, which sits medial to the arm.

Pitfall: the head points 'inward' whichever way you turn the bone, so it can't tell front from back; pair it with a front/back landmark such as the olecranon fossa (posterior).

Text: Of the humerus, the {{c1::distal::proximal or distal}} end is the part you can easily feel through the skin.
Back Extra:
Why: the proximal end sits inside the shoulder joint, buried under the deltoid and rotator cuff, while at the elbow the two epicondyles lie just under the skin.
